deliverables_scope.text: bilities by the U.S. Government. CONTEXT The USAF’s ability to efficiently and effectively operate at the edge of a battle area is essential to our superiority. Forward Operating Bases and Contingency Locations, also known as FOBs and CLs, respectively, are located at or near the edge and act as non-enduring locations to sustain operations conducted for the protection of national interests. For this Challenge, we’re seeking net-new solutions, enhancements to existing solutions, and the development of multi-capable solutions. Within each focus area, the USAF has identified a set of desired capabilities. Please note that these are not requirements but are offered to clarify USAF intent. Additionally, the list of desirable capabilities provided here should not be considered comprehensive. While participants may submit one or more solutions for each focus area, the same solution may not be submitted in multiple focus areas. FOCUS AREA DESCRIPTIONS Based on internal knowledge and market research conducted across the DoD, industry, and academia, the USAF has identified three focus areas to bring structure to the crowdsourcing process for this Challenge, as follows: Focus Area 1 Site & Logistics Optimization This focus area plays a crucial role in the USAF's efforts to establish

ive maintenance integration of multi-service and allied assets (an ally is any nation with which the U.S. is engaged in a common military effort or has entered into a common defensive military alliance) - Provision of real-time data and visibility into supply chain and pro- positioned assets FA2280-23-S-C001-002 Page 5 Focus Area 2 Training Modernization The USAF recognizes that the modernization of training is critical to meeting the ACE scheme of maneuver. The USAF needs to be agile and flexible in the face of evolving threats, with the ability to rapidly deploy and operate in austere and contested environments. To meet these requirements, the USAF must modernize its training approach to better prepare personnel. One way the USAF is modernizing its training is using simulation and virtual training environments. This allows personnel to train in realistic scenarios that simulate ACE challenges and complexities. Deploying modern training tools helps personnel develop the skills and competencies needed to operate effectively in these environments. As an example, the USAF is exploring the use of artificial intelligence and machine learning to enhance training programs and improve decision-making in real-time. Additionally, the USAF is investing in advanced communicati

ing activities across various locations. The USAF is also expanding its partnerships with other services and coalition partners to provide more opportunities for joint and multinational training. This approach helps Airmen develop the skills and competencies needed to work effectively in joint and multinational operations, which are critical to achieving ACE. Capabilities and/or technologies of interest, including but not limited to: - Culture of Learning: - Internal design of incentive programs - Implementation of effective augmented and virtual reality training programs - Team-Based Learning: - Standardization of training requirements for increased proficiencies - Development of crew training interoperability to develop special capabilities within teams - Development of intuitive and gamified training to reduce certification timelines for multi-capable Airmen - Student-led training to increase engagement and buy-in - Training visibility to improve crew member selection FA2280-23-S-C001-002 Page 6 - Joint Force Training: - Joint intelligence training (JIT) between military services, on demand and at the contested edge - Organized pre-positioning of supplies and equipment in multiple locations to improve access and supply chain resiliency - Augmentation of h

sla_onsite.text: ===== FILE: files/01.15.2025_Expedient_Basing_Challenge.pdf ===== FA2280-23-S-C001-002 Page 1 Expedient Basing Challenge Focus Areas 1-3 #expedientbasing BLUF The United States Air Force (USAF) is seeking modern capabilities to establish distributed operations in austere environments around the world where it must rapidly respond to humanitarian crises, natural disasters, and/or military activity. GENERAL INTENT The Contractor shall provide all labor, materials, equipment, supervision, and incidentals necessary to furnish and install a Building Automation System (BAS) to support integration and monitoring of existing building systems at the Guam Community-Based Outpatient Clinic (CBOC) and the American Samoa CBOC. This project is a straight-to-construction (StC) NRM project and is intended to implement a scalable BAS architecture focused on monitoring and alarming, with future capability to expand into full control wit

ance outages and costs, enhance energy management capabilities, and strengthen VAPIHCS’s ability to maintain safe, high reliability organization (HRO) across geographically dispersed locations. Due to the remote nature of these sites and limited availability of on-island technical resources, the absence of BAS currently delays detection and response to system failures, increasing the risk of impacts to clinical operations. A BAS mitigates these risks by providing early detection and alarming of system anomalies, improving preventive maintenance timeliness, reducing system downtime, and supporting compliance with environmental and operational requirements for healthcare spaces. Centralized remote monitoring will allow VAPIHCS FMS to proactively manage building systems and coordinate off-island technical support without reliance on emergency site visits, improving continuity of care and overall facility resilience. 2. forms_signatures.text: ===== FILE: files/36C26126R0040_2.docx ===== A.3 PRICE/COST SCHEDULE ITEM INFORMATION STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW) Modernization of Outlying CBOC Building Automation Systems (BAS) VAPIHCS – Guam CBOC and American Samoa CBOC 1. GENERAL INTENT The Contractor shall provide all labor, materials, equipment, supervision, and incidentals necessary to furnish and install a Building Automation System (BAS) to support integration and monitoring of existing building systems at the Guam Community-Based Outpatient Clinic (CBOC) and the American Samoa CBOC. This project is a straight-to-construction (StC) NRM project and is intended to implement a scalable BAS architecture focused on monitoring and alarming, with future capability to expand into full control without replacement of installed infrastructure. The BAS shall provide centralized and remote monitoring from VAPIHCS Honolulu, enabling proactive maintenance, improved system reliability, and enhanced operational visibility for geographically dispersed facilities. Description: This project will install a Building Automated System (BAS) at VAPIHCS outlying CBOCs in Guam and American Samoa to provide centralized, remote monitoring and control of critical building systems, including HVAC, domestic water, electrical systems, solar infrastructure, emergency power and life safety systems, and other systems supporting sensitive healthcare spaces. Justification: Implementation of a BAS will improve operational reliability, reduce corrective maintenance outages and costs, enhance energy management capabilities, and strengthen VAPIHCS’s ability to maintain safe, high reliability organization (HRO) across geographically dispersed locations. subcontracting_consortium.text: mination_of_Controlled_Unclassified_Information_CUI_Building_Information.docx ===== Safeguarding and Dissemination of Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) Building Information Certain information contained in the Solicitation Documents may have been designated as Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) building information. With respect to such information, Offerors shall agree to the terms as a condition of receipt such information, as set forth in this clause. This clause applies to all recipients of CUI building information (which falls within the CUI Physical Security category), including offerors, bidders, awardees, contractors, subcontractors, lessors, suppliers and manufacturers. Marking CUI: Contractors must submit any contractor-generated documents that contain building information to GSA for review and identification of any CUI building information that may be included. In addition, any documents GSA identifies as containing CUI building information must be marked in accordance with the Order and the Marking Controlled Unclassified Information Handbook (the current version may be found at https://www.archives.gov/files/cui/20161206-cui-marking-handbook-v1-1.pdf) before the original or any copies are disseminated to any other parties. If CUI content is identified, the CO ma

the original documents and all copies, before any dissemination, or authorized GSA employees may mark the documents. 1. Authorized recipients: a. Building information designated as CUI must be protected with access strictly controlled and limited to those individuals having a Lawful Government Purpose to access such information, as defined in 32 C.F.R. § 2002.4(bb). Those with such a Lawful Government Purpose may include Federal, state and local government entities, and non-governmental entities engaged in the conduct of business on behalf of or with GSA. DESIGN-BUILD OBJECTIVES The Contractor shall: a. Coordinate with the BIA-Colville Agency COR to schedule a site visit and conduct field investigations. b. Perform full design analysis including heating/cooling loads, airflow calculations, duct compatibility, electrical capacity evaluation, and refrigerant line assessments. c. Design an HVAC system meeting current industry standards, Washington State building codes, energy efficiency requirements (minimum 19+ SEER), and the operational needs of the facility. d. Develop construction drawings, technical specifications, product data sheets, and submittals for Government approval prior to construction. e. Provide design justification demonstrating that the proposed system meets required capacity, efficiency, and performance criteria. f. Remove existing HVAC components in accordance with environmental and hazardous material regulations. g. Construct and install the new HVAC system per the approved design package. h. Commission the completed system, perform airflow balancing, leak checks, refrigerant charging, testing, and final tuning. i.

Component 3:  Enabling Private Sector Engagement in Renewable Energy

The activities under this component will be led by PENRA, in coordination with DISCOs, relevant line ministries, and local commercial banks. The subcomponent related to health facilities will be implemented by PENRA in coordination with the Ministry of Health.

This component focuses on the reinforcement of infrastructure to enable the evacuation of utility scale projects (sub component 3.1) and a scale up of rooftop solar PV systems for health, SMEs and residential sector (sub component 3.2/3.3/3.4/3.5). In addition, under sub-component 3.6 a pilot for battery recycling will be launched, whereas sub component 3.7 will be related to design and pilot of a liquidity support facility for PETL. The component is likely to have moderate E&S impacts except under sub-component 3.6, where the E&S impacts are considered to be substantial. ies for Rapid Adoption (ASTRA) ARA NUMBER: ARA FA8750-23-S-7007 CATALOG OF FEDERAL DOMESTIC ASSISTANCE (CFDA) Number: N/A I. TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENTS: The Air Force Research Laboratory is soliciting white papers under this Advanced Research Announcement (ARA) for research, development, integration, test and evaluation of technologies/techniques to enable the rapid integration of Systems of Systems (SoS) and the auto generation of tests of the System-of-systems Technology Integration Tool Chain for Heterogeneous Electronic Systems (STITCHES) subsystem specifications and properties. White papers shall: Describe methods to develop, implement, and demonstrate a software prototype of a SoS that will provide increased military effectiveness, cost leverage (i.e., the cost of the opponent to counter relative to the cost of the U.S. to deploy), and adaptability relative to the current platform-centric approach; Outline the development and provide a system architecting approach to achieve rapid integration of new U.S. technologies as they are developed, without requiring significant re-engineering of existing capabilities, systems, or systems of systems; Outline how to implement applicable Open System Architect

operate (ATO) issued by the Department of Defense (DoD); Provide system-level user identity and access management, and application-level single sign-on (SSO); Establish a repository and backup and restore all ecosystem data; Develop a graphical user interface system for web-based utilization of the toolchain and users with limited toolchain experience; and Design, implement, and integrate secure cloud-based hosting in multiple levels and provide the ability for the secure transfer of files between different levels.
